name: 32228-batchdecode-qwen3next80bfp8-tp4
model: Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8, the checkpoint's own FP8 release. Ungated; ~77 GB of weights.
parallelism: TP=4, EP off, PP=1, DP=1. One node, one server, no external cache tier.
architecture: Qwen3NextForCausalLM, ~80B total / ~3B active, a hybrid linear-attention MoE; the rest is in the checkpoint's own config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=200, warmup the first 25%, bounded at 4000 requests with a 1800 s safety cap.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no shared prefix: 256 prompt tokens in, 128 output tokens out, both fixed with no spread, `ignore_eos: true` and `temperature: 0.0` set in `backend.extras.body`. Prompts are unique. Seed 32228.
purpose: An 80-billion-parameter chat assistant giving short fixed-length replies to 200 concurrent users on four GPUs.
launch:
# sglang server arguments. Flat `key: value` only -- a nested block is DROPPED by the reader.
# host/port/served-model-name are set by the serving layer, not here.

model-path: Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8

tp-size: 4

# The checkpoint ships custom modelling code.
trust-remote-code: true

# Far above anything this workload reaches (a request occupies 384 tokens), and written down
# because the engine sizes its pools from this number rather than from the requests.
context-length: 16384

# The recurrent-state pool is held at a fixed budget rather than auto-fitted to whatever memory
# happens to be free at launch.
mamba-radix-cache-strategy: extra_buffer_lazy
mamba-track-interval: 256
max-mamba-cache-size: 96

mem-fraction-static: 0.8
enable-cache-report: true
